advisory.finding: The new test covers 'archived_duplicate_target' but omits the documented 'deleted' replacement case, even though _is_live_ticket treats deleted and archived via different code paths (state.get('archived') vs status in {'archived','deleted'}). A deleted-target regression could pass unnoticed.
merged_from: `escalated` is a member of _NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES but no test case exercises close_class='escalated'; the parametrization only covers 'not_a_bug' and 'duplicate' for the skip path, leaving one of the three exempt classes uncovered.

The `escalated` close class — one of the three members of `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` that the bypass keys on — is never exercised in any test case (neither a skip nor a block direction), so removing `escalated` from the exemption set would not fail any test.

The 'deleted / unresolvable replacement does not bypass' contract is untested: `_is_live_ticket` treats `error`, `status=='deleted'`, and an unresolved id as non-live via branches distinct from `archived`, but only the `archived` target is exercised.

No test exercises the 'net-active links only' contract by linking then removing (unlink) a replacement — the block cases either never link (`no_relation`) or link in the wrong direction/class, so a regression that read stale/removed links as active would not be caught.

The `supersedes` inbound branch's liveness check on the superseding ticket is untested for a non-live (archived/deleted) replacement: the only non-live-target case (`archived_duplicate_target`) covers the `duplicates` branch, so the `_is_live_ticket(link['from_id'])` guard on the supersedes path has no negative test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm and document whether a closed replacement target should count as 'live' for the bypass, and add a test pinning the chosen behavior.
evidence: transition_close.py:51: `and state.get("status") not in {"archived", "deleted"}`
docs/ticket-model.md:81: `... link to a live ticket ...` (does not state whether a closed target qualifies)
advisory.finding: A closed (but not archived/deleted) replacement ticket counts as 'live' and bypasses verification, since _is_live_ticket only rejects status in {archived, deleted}. This policy edge (a bug pointing at an already-closed duplicate still skips completion) is neither documented explicitly nor covered by a test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-validate `_has_live_replacement_link` under the write lock (or re-check replacement liveness immediately before `txn.transition_core`) so a replacement archived/deleted in the verify->close window cannot yield a stale bypass.
evidence: transition_close.py:206 `if _has_live_replacement_link(ticket_id, ticket_type, close_class, tracker): return None` — the bypass returns from `_completion_precheck`, which close_ticket runs OUTSIDE the write lock (transition_close.py:520-546 comment: 'runs OUTSIDE the write lock since an LLM call must not serialize all writes').
The locked write happens later at transition_close.py:554 `txn.transition_core(...)`; nothing re-checks `_has_live_replacement_link` after acquiring the lock.

Contrast: the signature path DOES re-validate the window — transition_close.py:585-591 re-reads HEAD (`_fresh_sha = _signing.head_sha(...)`) and skips attestation on drift. The bypass path has no analogous freshness recheck.
_is_live_ticket resolves liveness at check time only (transition_close.py:40-52); a concurrent `archive`/`delete` of the target between the check and the commit is not detected.
advisory.finding: The replacement-liveness bypass check runs outside the write lock and is not re-validated before the locked close commits (TOCTOU). A replacement/canonical ticket that is live at check time can be archived or deleted in the verify->close window, so the bug closes as a 'replaced' non-completion disposition while its replacement no longer exists — skipping the billable completion verifier against a stale link state.
scenarios: Concurrent process (or the same agent in a follow-up op) archives/deletes the canonical/replacement ticket between the precheck and the locked transition_core write.
A long verify->close window (the module notes transport retries/timeouts widen it, :576-579) increases the odds the replacement changes state mid-close.
